india: Emergency fund (6 months expenses) in savings/liquid fund
Low-cost index fund SIP (monthly, long term)
Only then: individual stocks, gold, REITs with small share
usa: Emergency fund (3-6 months) in high-yield savings
Health insurance (+ term life if dependents)
Low-cost index ETFs in taxable account; stocks only with small share

options.name: Savings account / Fixed Deposit (FD)
options.returns: Roughly 3-7.5% a year; check the bank's current rate
options.tax: Interest taxed at your slab rate; TDS above limits
options.where: Any bank; small finance banks often pay more (DICGC insures up to Rs 5 lakh per bank)
options.note: Safe but may barely beat inflation. Good for emergency fund and goals under 3 years.

options.name: PPF (Public Provident Fund)
options.returns: Govt-set rate reviewed quarterly, ~7-8% historically; tax-free
options.tax: EEE under old regime: deposit, interest and maturity tax-free
options.note: Sovereign-backed. Strong debt anchor for long-term goals.

options.name: EPF / VPF
options.min: 12% of basic (VPF lets you add more)
options.tax: Interest tax-free up to contribution limits
options.where: Through your employer; manage on the EPFO portal
options.note: If salaried, you already have this. VPF is a cheap safe top-up.

options.name: NPS (National Pension System)
options.returns: Market-linked; equity/debt mix, ~8-12% long-run range, not guaranteed
options.tax: Extra Rs 50,000 deduction (80CCD(1B), old regime); employer share benefits
options.where: Bank, or app like Protean/KFintech via eNPS
options.note: Very low cost retirement account. Rules change; check current ones.

options.name: Index funds / ETFs via SIP
options.returns: Nifty 50 long-run ~10-13% a year with big ups and downs; can fall 30%+ in a crash
options.tax: Equity gains: short-term (<1 yr) and long-term (>1 yr) rates differ; check current rates
options.where: Direct plans on Zerodha Coin, Groww, Kuvera, or AMC sites
options.note: Best default for beginners: cheap, diversified, automatic. Prefer Direct plans with low expense ratio.

options.name: Actively managed mutual funds
options.returns: Varies; many fail to beat index after fees over 10 years
options.note: Check 10-year record vs index, expense ratio, fund manager tenure.

options.name: Direct stocks (NSE / BSE)
options.returns: Unlimited upside and total loss both possible
options.tax: STCG / LTCG apply; check current rates
options.where: Zerodha, Groww, Upstox, ICICI Direct (SEBI-registered brokers only)
options.note: Study first (Varsity Module 1-4). Keep to a small slice until you can read financial statements.

options.name: Gold: Sovereign Gold Bonds, Gold ETFs
options.liquidity: ETF high; SGB tradable on exchange but thin
options.lockin: SGB 8 yrs (exit from yr 5); ETF none
options.returns: Tracks gold price; long-run hedge vs inflation, can be flat for years
options.tax: Differs by instrument; SGB maturity gains tax-free for original buyers
options.where: Broker for ETF; SGB mostly via secondary market (new issues have been paused)
options.note: 5-10% of portfolio at most. Avoid jewellery as an investment (making charges).

options.name: Government bonds & T-bills (RBI Retail Direct)
options.note: Direct sovereign lending without a middleman.

options.name: REITs / InvITs
options.where: Any stock broker (Embassy, Mindspace, Brookfield REITs)
options.note: Real estate exposure without buying a flat.

options.name: US stocks / ETFs from India (LRS)
options.returns: S&P 500 long-run ~10% in USD; add INR drift and fees
options.tax: Foreign gains taxed in India; TCS on remittance; check current rules
options.where: INDmoney, Vested, or Interactive Brokers under RBI LRS (USD 250,000 per year limit)
options.note: Adds currency diversification. Read tax and TCS rules before starting.

options.name: High-yield savings / CDs
options.returns: Tracks Fed rates; check current APY
options.where: Online banks (FDIC insured up to $250,000 per depositor, per bank)
options.note: Home for emergency fund and goals under 3 years.

options.name: Treasuries, T-bills, I-Bonds
options.returns: Current Treasury yield; I-Bond rate = fixed + inflation
options.tax: Federal tax only, no state tax
options.note: Backed by US govt. Good for safe portion of portfolio.

options.name: 401(k) / 403(b)
options.returns: Depends on funds chosen; pick low-cost index/target-date funds
options.tax: Traditional: pre-tax, taxed on withdrawal. Roth: after-tax, tax-free growth
options.note: Always take the full employer match first: it is free money.

options.name: IRA / Roth IRA
options.tax: Roth: tax-free growth. Income limits apply; annual contribution cap
options.note: Great tax shelter if you qualify. Check current-year limits on IRS.gov.

options.name: Index ETFs (VTI, VOO, VXUS)
options.returns: US stocks ~10% a year long-run nominal; drops of 30-50% happen
options.tax: Long-term (>1 yr) gains taxed lower than short-term
options.note: Beginner default: total market + international, expense ratio under 0.1%.

options.name: Individual stocks
options.returns: Wide range; most individual stocks underperform the index
options.note: Keep it to a small slice until you can analyse a company.

options.name: Bond funds (BND, AGG)
options.returns: Roughly current yield; prices fall when rates rise
options.note: Cushions stock drops; match duration to your timeline.

options.name: REITs (VNQ)
options.tax: Dividends mostly ordinary income; best in IRA

glossary.def: Fund that copies a market index (Nifty 50, S&P 500) at very low cost.
Systematic Investment Plan: fixed amount invested automatically each month.
Yearly fee a fund charges, as % of your money. Lower is better.
Spreading money across assets so one failure does not sink you.
Earning returns on past returns. Time matters more than amount.
Price divided by earnings per share. Rough gauge of how expensive a stock is.
Yearly rise in prices. Returns below inflation lose buying power.
Split of your money between stocks, bonds, gold, cash.
Resetting your split to target once a year.
Prolonged rise / fall of 20% or more.
Share of company profit paid to shareholders.
Net Asset Value: price of one mutual fund unit.
How much a price swings. Higher swings = higher risk.
How fast you can turn an asset into cash without losing value.
